name: Nethaniah
overview: Nethaniah is a biblical figure associated with multiple roles and lineages. He is identified as the father of Ishmael, who played a significant part in the political turmoil following the Babylonian conquest by assassinating Gedaliah, the Babylonian-appointed governor (2 Kings 25:23, 25). Additionally, Nethaniah is noted as a Levite and a chief temple musician, serving under the lineage of Asaph and holding a leadership role among the temple singers (1 Chronicles 25:2, 12). He also appears as a Levite appointed by King Jehoshaphat to accompany princes tasked with teaching the law in Judah, highlighting his involvement in religious instruction and worship (2 Chronicles 17:8). Furthermore, Nethaniah is mentioned as the father of Jehudi, who was sent to retrieve the prophetic scroll from Baruch, indicating a connection to prophetic ministry (Jeremiah 36:14). These references collectively portray Nethaniah as a figure of both spiritual leadership and familial significance within the biblical narrative.
